name: Workspaces, roles, and invitations

requirements.text: Every user receives a personal workspace and active-workspace pointer.
Existing owned resources are backfilled to the personal workspace without losing creator attribution.
Users create and switch workspaces, and invalid active pointers are repaired deterministically.
Owners may invite admin or member; admins may invite only member; neither may invite owner.
Invitations use one-time URLs, expire after seven days, and can be listed, resent, revoked, or replaced.
Acceptance requires an authenticated non-suspended matching-email user and atomically creates one membership.
Owners and admins manage only the member roles permitted by the role matrix and cannot invalidate the owner invariant.
Non-members cannot forge active workspace selection or access workspace resources.
Guest/viewer roles, SSO/SCIM, workspace deletion, and audit-log exports remain future-depth features.
Ownership transfer requires password confirmation, an existing member target, atomic role exchange, and an audit record.
Member-capacity checks include unexpired invitations and lock the workspace while reserving capacity.

externalPrerequisites: Configured mail transport for invitation email delivery

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every migrated owner and resource maps to exactly one valid personal workspace before legacy ownership is contracted.
Role authorization matches the owner/admin/member matrix for content, integrations, members, and billing.
Invitation acceptance is race-safe, email-bound, expiring, and idempotent.

observedBehaviors: Workspaces are listed with role and member information.

implementationEvidence.description: Workspace migration, context, role authorization, membership, invitations, transfer, capacity, audit, billing, custom-domain, and webhook coverage passed in the complete Laravel suite (218 tests, 10,891 assertions). Focused regressions passed for analytics workspace scoping (1 test/12 assertions), shared-workspace overlay consent (9/94), and active-workspace link-insight/QR isolation (8/81).

implementationEvidence.description: A populated disposable SQLite copy was rolled back and re-applied across the three workspace ownership migrations. Legacy-column SHA-256 row-streams matched for 18 application tables; personal subscription values matched after owner normalization. The resulting copy retained 2 users, 2 personal workspaces, 2 owner memberships, and 2 subscriptions; all nine workspace-owned tables had zero unassigned rows; SQLite integrity_check returned ok and foreign_key_check returned zero violations. The original disposable app database was not modified.
implementationEvidence.reference: Disposable populated SQLite database copy; migrate:rollback --step=3 --path=database/migrations followed by migrate --path=database/migrations

implementationEvidence.description: At localhost:8101, an owner created a workspace and invited admin/member accounts; an admin accepted the owner-issued invitation. The workspace-admin view showed no Resend/Revoke controls for a pending owner-issued admin invitation while a pending member invitation retained both. The owner transfer form opened and was cancelled without submission; workspace settings at 390x844 had no horizontal overflow or browser errors.

A workspace member saw a webhook summary without endpoint URL or signing secret; direct delivery-history access returned HTTP 403. Owner and workspace-admin billing views were compared at localhost:8101; only the owner had plan-change controls.

Current Task 3 workspace suites passed inside the focused run, including backfill/contract chronology, membership and role authorization, invitation lifecycle, ownership transfer, capacity locking semantics, tenant scoping, and append-only workspace audit records.
implementationEvidence.reference: tests/Feature/Workspaces; Task 3 focused run (363 passed, 1 skipped, 4166 assertions)
